discovery: Discovery of the neodymium-iron-boron (Nd2Fe14B) permanent magnet
subfield: Condensed matter physics / magnetism and magnetic materials
motivation: In 1982-1984 Masato Sagawa, by sintering, and John Croat, by rapid melt-spinning, independently discovered that the tetragonal compound Nd2Fe14B combines the large magnetization of iron with the strong uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy of the rare-earth 4f shell. Conventional wisdom held that iron-rich rare-earth compounds were unusable because of short Fe-Fe distances and low Curie temperatures; boron stabilised a new crystal structure and overturned this belief. The result is the strongest permanent magnet known, with a maximum energy product far beyond samarium-cobalt, made from comparatively abundant elements. It deepened the physics of exchange and crystal-field anisotropy in 3d-4f intermetallics and coercivity mechanisms, and it now underpins electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, hard-disk drives and MRI. Like the blue LED, this is materials discovery that transformed both physics and society, and it is still fully worthy of recognition.
